summary.oneLiner: Max India's three verticals are inflecting together: consolidated quarterly loss shrank to ₹6.8cr (from ₹27.8cr in Q3 and ₹35.5cr YoY) on 45% QoQ / 58% YoY revenue growth, Noida finally received a partial occupancy certificate unlocking ~₹150cr of stuck receivables and a Phase-2 re-filing, and both AGEasy (management-guided EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27) and Care Homes (consolidated EBITDA breakeven guided H1 FY28) have visible paths to profitability as newly added beds/products mature. Management continues to defend that the ~₹1,000cr market cap materially undervalues the sum-of-parts.

one-line thesis: Max India's three verticals are inflecting together: consolidated quarterly loss shrank to ₹6.8cr (from ₹27.8cr in Q3 and ₹35.5cr YoY) on 45% QoQ / 58% YoY revenue growth, Noida finally received a partial occupancy certificate unlocking ~₹150cr of stuck receivables and a Phase-2 re-filing, and both AGEasy (management-guided EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27) and Care Homes (consolidated EBITDA breakeven guided H1 FY28) have visible paths to profitability as newly added beds/products mature. Management continues to defend that the ~₹1,000cr market cap materially undervalues the sum-of-parts.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > No one-off items called out on the headline P&L this quarter; note the pending ₹32cr tax demand (Antara Purukul/Dehradun lease-accounting dispute) is NOT yet in the numbers — management expects it to reverse to near-zero on rectification (precedent: last year's ₹11cr demand was cut to ₹1.62cr).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: AGEasy: exit monthly revenue run-rate guided at ₹14–16cr for the current year (FY27); "high-growth year" reiterated; EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 (last quarter of this year).

Care Homes: consolidated EBITDA breakeven guided for H1 FY28 (unit-level: 4–6 quarters to contribution-margin breakeven at 40–45% occupancy; 8–10 quarters to 65–70% occupancy where EBITDA margin reaches 16–18%; ROCE target 25–26%).

Residences/real estate: committed to 1.5msf/year cadence — FY26 delivered only 1.1msf (missed by 0.4msf after the Chandigarh project lost height clearance post "Operation Sindoor"). Three new opportunities in pipeline (Sector-105 Noida intergenerational ~1.1msf, one Bangalore, one Dehradun) expected to close this year, totalling ~2msf — management says this "catches up" the deficit.

Noida Phase 2: re-filing to follow completion of Phase-1 possession obligations + Noida Authority recertification of revised building plans; sales expected to start "sometime during FY27". Pricing assumed at ₹16,000–18,000/sqft (2-3x last sale), implying ~₹700cr+ revenue potential on the balance ~4.4 lakh sqft.
Estate 361 Phase 2 (remaining 180 of 360 units): launch "around the corner" / "very very soon" — 141 of 180 Phase-1 units sold as of call date.

Path to profitability (group): management expects 1–2 verticals to show profitability in "later part of FY27"; explicitly declined to give a harder date, citing geopolitical uncertainty and minimum-wage revisions across states.
Fundraise: comfortable on cash for next 3–6 months; awaiting better market sentiment before diluting; an announcement expected "sometime this year".
Labour Code impact: ₹3–4cr P&L hit across all entities in FY27 (mostly gratuity provisioning), already accounted for.
order book & pipeline: Estate 360 (Gurgaon, fully sold): ITD collections ₹534cr, 87% collection efficiency since inception; total management fee earned till 31-Mar-26 ₹45.6cr (₹26cr accrued in FY26); ultimate total mgmt fee estimated ~₹130cr over full project cycle.

Estate 361: 1.04msf / 360 units; Phase-1 (180 units) launched Dec-25 — 127 bookings at March-end, 141 sold as of call date (May-26), collections ₹69cr; total mgmt fee estimated ~₹200cr over the project cycle (price-dependent, sales still ongoing).

Noida (ContendBuilders SPV): partial occupancy certificate received for 3 towers post-Supreme Court/authority clearance — unlocks receivables of ~₹150cr+; nearly all mgmt fee already recognized except ~₹14cr of possession-linked payments; ~220 units / 0.44msf still to be developed for Phase 2; ~₹70–75cr of construction spend remaining (largely pending bills — construction itself essentially complete).
Sector-wide residences target: 1.5msf/year commitment; 3 new projects (Sector-105 Noida, Bangalore, Dehradun) in advanced discussion, ~2msf combined.
segment / subsidiary detail: Dehradun residence (mature, cash-generative): Q4 revenue ₹6.7cr; FY26 total revenue ₹24.2cr, profit ₹2.3cr; 5 unit releases in the year added ~₹1.7cr marketing fee; community fully occupied — growth now more linear; cash-positive and profitable.

Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes): 485 beds across 8 homes (NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai); 1 Gurgaon home (28 beds) under renovation, near-live. ~3,400 patients served in Q4FY26, ~50,000 since inception. Segment revenue ₹11.4cr in Q4 (1.1x QoQ); FY26 revenue ₹38.8cr (1.6x YoY). Occupancy up ~10% QoQ on already-operational beds (e.g., Sector-41 26%→34%, Noida 13%→38%, Bannerghatta 10%→37%); contribution margin improving sharply (Noida –19%→+6% QoQ; Gurgaon Sector-41 –43%→–17%; Gurgaon Sector-24 –13%→–5%). Customer voice score 90.2% in Q4 (broadly flat QoQ), 92–93% for the full year. Care-at-Home merged into Care Homes to share infrastructure/staff and improve unit economics.

AGEasy (senior-wellness D2C/marketplace platform): Q4 net revenue ₹23cr (+1.4x YoY, +1.2x QoQ); FY26 revenue ~₹77cr (+100% YoY). RoAS (Return on Ad Spend) improved to 1.8 blended, exiting March-26 at 2.9; D2C RoAS alone moved from 0.7–0.8 to 1.7–1.8 over the year; marketplace RoAS moved from ~1 to ~2. Satisfaction index 87% in Q4 vs 83% in Q3, 84% FY vs 82% prior year. ~91 products / 159 SKUs; launched Gut-health condition category (4 new products with Wellbeing Nutrition) plus 19 new products in FY26 overall, 65% of which deliver ≥50% gross margin. Sourcing mix: 70% domestic / 30% import (mainly China). ~7 lakh+ lives touched, 44,000 repeat customers, NPS 45. Blended online gross margin improved from 38% (start of year) to 46% (Q4FY26).
growth verticals / optionality: AGEasy expanding beyond nutraceuticals into wearables/technology for seniors (boAt partnership — watch product underperformed expectations, now working on other tech-based solutions); IIT-Delhi co-innovation on wheelchairs (now a meaningful revenue line); Star Union Dai-Ichi Life Insurance tie-up on senior wellness/financial literacy.
Piloting an "integrated wellness clinic" (modern medicine + Ayurveda/Acupressure) at one residence — if successful, to be rolled out across all communities as a differentiator.
Talks ongoing for new intergenerational communities beyond Gurgaon/Noida — North and South India footprint expansion flagged but undisclosed pending signed agreements.

GEO/SEO (AI-search) positioning called out as a tailwind rather than a threat for AGEasy's category — company says it is an early, "relatively unexplored" opportunity to lower customer acquisition cost even as Gemini-driven search disrupts other e-commerce categories.
6a. moat & competitive position: Management explicitly frames its patent portfolio as "the biggest moat": 3 patents granted, 3 more filed for AGEasy products; positions differentiated/patented product development as the basis for pricing power and category leadership.

Antara Assisted Care became the first assisted-living provider in India to secure NABH care-home accreditation (2 homes certified) — a regulatory/quality barrier competitors (fragmented small vendors, and larger hospital-led players like Max Healthcare in Care-at-Home) do not yet clear.

On Care-at-Home specifically, management conceded there is "not much differentiation apart from trained certified staff" versus fragmented small vendors — hence the deliberate move to fold it into Care Homes rather than compete on scale there.
margins & cost dynamics: AGEasy: China-sourced raw material and logistics costs pressured by "current geopolitical situation"; mitigated via alternate Indian vendors, larger forward orders to lock pricing/supply, alternate logistics routing, and selective price increases on affected SKUs — no significant margin impact seen through Q4 and the current quarter, but management continues to monitor closely.

Care Homes: 32%+ contribution margin and 16–18% EBITDA margin targeted at maturity per home; Senior Living residence projects targeted at 20%+ IRR and 10–12% PAT margin per project; AGEasy targeted at 16–18% EBITDA margin within "another 2–3 years."
Labour Code wage-revision impact quantified at ₹3–4cr across entities in FY27 (mostly gratuity provisioning — a notional/non-cash entry).

Staff-cost concern raised by an investor: ₹80–90cr payroll on ~₹200cr reported turnover — management's response is that reported top line is structurally understated because SPV-level real-estate sales (Estate 360/361, routed through Max Estates) don't consolidate as a revenue line, only as net P&L share.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Chandigarh residence project slipped: lost height clearance after "Operation Sindoor" (India-Pakistan escalation reference) — one of the reasons FY26 residential delivery (1.1msf) missed the 1.5msf target.
Noida Phase-2 re-filing is capex-light (existing land) but gated entirely on government/authority plan-revalidation — timing not in management's control.
~₹70–75cr of pending construction bills remain for existing Noida Phase-1 towers (physical construction essentially complete; only finishing/bill settlement left).
New bed additions for Care Homes are on hold until existing (recently added) beds mature to the model — next evaluation window flagged for October–November 2026.
capital allocation: Fundraise under evaluation but deliberately deferred pending better market sentiment ("no point diluting at a value which is not conducive"); 3–6 months of cash runway cited as comfortable.
Equity to be deployed primarily into growing Care Homes and Antara Senior Living projects.
Estate 360/361 equity investments structured to return capital after ~4 years at 1.5–1.6x.
risks & watch-items: Pending ₹32cr income-tax demand (Antara Purukul/Dehradun lease-accounting dispute) from a faceless assessment that allegedly failed to credit brought-forward losses — rectification filed, precedent (₹11cr → ₹1.62cr last year) supports management's expectation it goes to near-zero, but not yet resolved.

Real-estate collections are structurally "lumpy" (front-loaded booking fees, then construction-linked tranches over ~3 quarters, becoming periodic only from FY28–29) — near-term reported EBITDA for the residences vertical can swing from positive to negative project-to-project.
China sourcing exposure (~30% of AGEasy inputs) to geopolitical/tariff and logistics cost risk.
Execution/approval risk on Noida Phase-2 (fully dependent on Noida Authority timeline) and on the 3 new residence-pipeline projects (Sector-105 Noida, Bangalore, Dehradun) not yet signed.
Broader macro: management flagged geopolitical impact and state-level minimum-wage revisions as headwinds already affecting parts of the business.
management quality / tone: Candid and quantitatively specific in Q&A (gave granular occupancy/contribution-margin walk-throughs by individual care home, disclosed exact management-fee estimates per project, and directly addressed an investor's pointed challenge on 10-year capital conservatism).

MD acknowledged the criticism on slow asset growth as "partially right," attributing lost time to COVID-era diversification, and reiterated conviction that current ~₹1,000cr market cap (vs. ~₹300cr at 2019-20 listing) still understates sum-of-parts value; committed to demonstrating this over "next 9 to 12 months."
Declined to give a hard date for group-level profitability, citing macro uncertainty — read as appropriately cautious rather than over-promising.
non-obvious takeaways: Real-estate segment revenue is structurally muted in consolidated reporting: SPV-level top line (Estate 360/361, sold in partnership with Max Estates) is NOT consolidated as revenue — only net P&L share — so headline turnover understates the scale of real activity (management fee run-rate math: ~₹10–12cr annuity income per 250-unit community once operational, split 60% CAM / 40% discretionary spend).

The Noida partial-occupancy-certificate breakthrough is a genuine catalyst: it both unlocks ~₹150cr of stuck receivables AND re-opens the Phase-2 approval pathway at pricing management says is now 2–3x the original Phase-1 sale price.

Management's framing of AI-driven search disruption (Gemini) as a net positive for AGEasy (GEO/SEO "relatively unexplored" for the senior-wellness category) is a contrarian read worth tracking against actual RoAS trends next quarter.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (this): First MAXIND note. Noida partial-OC received (₹150cr+ receivable unlock); consolidated loss narrowed sharply (₹6.8cr vs ₹27.8cr Q3, ₹35.5cr Q4FY25); AGEasy FY26 revenue +100% YoY to ~₹77cr; Care Homes bed base at 485, occupancy/contribution-margin inflecting on maturing cohorts; FY26 residential delivery missed 1.5msf target (delivered 1.1msf) due to Chandigarh clearance loss.

Q1 FY27 → check: AGEasy monthly run-rate vs ₹14–16cr guide; Noida Phase-2 re-filing progress/authority approval; Estate 361 Phase-2 (180 units) launch; resolution of ₹32cr tax demand; fundraise announcement; any new bed additions (management said evaluation starts Oct-Nov).
